title: Void Ending in a Sextile to Neptune
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The sextile is one of the two friendly aspects. Picatrix ties the Moon to the fortunes by trine and sextile whenever a work is meant to prosper, and grades the sextile as the aspect of moderate friendship: the signs it joins are kin in action but not in passion, so the concord between them is a lukewarm one.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a sextile to Neptune, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his drifting mist. Neptune is unknown to Picatrix; the planet was found in 1846, by calculation before anyone saw it, and the source never mentions it. Any reading of it here is this almanac's extension of the lunar doctrine, not the doctrine itself. Named for the Greek lord of the sea, it is read as cold, blue, and dissolving: a course that closes on it ends in something misty, where edges soften and matters drift rather than conclude.
